notes.title: Major Update – Demon Core, Free Rerolls & More!
notes.content:
[p]Here comes another big optimization list for everyone![/p][hr][/hr][h2]🆕 New “Demonic” Insectoid Core[/h2][p]A brand-new elemental core has arrived![/p][list][*][p]Its synergy effect [b]replaces \[Rage Attack] with a short transformation[/b], granting bonus final damage.
[i](Who said Rage Attacks are useless in the late game? Now you transform instead!)[/i][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/8af07e572a91923dd6e98888a23f5de071318e21.gif"][/img][/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]🎮 Gameplay[/h2][list][*][p][b]\[New][/b] Added new Dual-Element Synergies: [b]Blood+Ice, Thunder+Wood, Demon+Ice, Demon+Thunder.[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Optimization][/b] Players now get [b]1 free reroll by default[/b] on Insectoid Core choices, and can unlock +2 rerolls via the talent tree. That’s up to [b]3 free rerolls[/b] per selection!
[i](In short: every time you pick from 3 Insectoid Cores, you can reroll up to 3 times for free — massively boosting your chances of finding the one you want!)[/i][/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Optimization][/b] In the Ultimate Equipment menu, you can now spend a small amount of [b]Dark Crystals[/b] to refresh the selection.[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[New][/b] Added a [b]Compendium function[/b] in the ESC menu! (Now you can check collections in-game. Locked entries will still stay hidden.)[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[New][/b] Added a [b]Core Ban System[/b] — ban up to 3 Insectoid Core types you don’t want! (Unlocks after clearing Difficulty 6 once.)[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Buff][/b] Fire Core synergies have been enhanced! (In short: overall damage buffs.)[/p][list][*][p]Lv.3: [b]Fireball[/b] now deals +60% → (up from 50%) [b]Critical Damage[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Lv.4: [b]Fireball[/b] has a 30% chance to inflict Burn, dealing [b]400%[/b] (up from 300%) Fireball damage over time.[/p][/*][*][p]Lv.5: Deal [b]100%[/b] (up from 50%) additional damage to Burned enemies.[/p][/*][*][p]Lv.6: [b]Fireball[/b] applies Flame Marks; at 10 stacks, triggers [i]Inferno Devastation[/i], dealing [b]1200%[/b] (up from 800%) Fireball damage.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]🌱 New Player / New Save Adjustments[/h2][list][*][p][b]\[Optimization][/b] Insectoid Core types now unlock gradually with progression and difficulty.[/p][list][*][p]At the start of a new save, only 6 core types are available. More will unlock as you advance.[/p][/*][*][p]Veteran players are unaffected.
[i](This makes it easier for new players to build effective runs without being overwhelmed.)[/i][/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]🎮 Controls & Feel[/h2][list][*][p][b]\[New][/b] Added controller vibration. (Try it out! You can disable it anytime in settings.)[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Optimization][/b] Reduced recovery time after Rage Attacks again — you can move sooner now![/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Optimization][/b] Slightly reduced the dash distance of the Shadow Blade’s light attacks. (Helps avoid unintentionally colliding with enemy attacks.)[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]✨ Visuals & FX[/h2][list][*][p][b]\[Fix][/b] Another attempt to fix flashing white screen issues when running on handheld devices.[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[New][/b] Skin selection menu now has [b]dynamic animations[/b]. (So bouncy!)[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[New][/b] Replaced icons for all equipment, making it easier to recognize effects at a glance.[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Optimization][/b] In the Core interface, only usable slots are displayed. (New players won’t be confused by “locked slots” anymore.)[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Optimization][/b] Enlarged controller button icons for better clarity.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]🏕️ Other[/h2][list][*][p][b]\[Optimization][/b] Adjusted camp map — characters now respawn at the camp center. (Less walking back.)[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Rework][/b] Save system rebuilt to prevent lost saves.[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Optimization][/b] Improved controller support, attempting compatibility with more controller types.[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Optimization][/b] Fixed vibration continuing when opening a window — it now stops properly.[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Optimization][/b] Improved selection UX for the resource exchanger.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]🐞 Bug Fixes[/h2][list][*][p][b]\[Fix][/b] Achievement could not be completed if you skipped shops globally — fixed.[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Fix][/b] Achievement/skin unlock for 60 Perfect Dodges was counting incorrectly — fixed.[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Fix][/b] Flashing white screen FX on handheld devices — fixed.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Regarding the issue of some players being unable to launch the game.
notes.content: [p]If you can’t launch the game, please try the following:[/p][p]- In your game library, find this game.[/p][p]- Right-click it and select Properties.[/p][p]- Click Browse Local Files.[/p][p]- In the folder that opens, delete the “BepInEx” and “dotnet” folders.[/p]

Today’s update is a small one, mainly focused on bug fixes and minor optimizations:[/p][hr][/hr][h3]🐞 Fixes & Optimizations[/h3][list][*][p][b]\[Fix][/b] Resolved an issue where [b]Elemental Orb shards[/b] would not appear.[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Optimization][/b] Ultimate Equipment: [b]“Grey Trade”[/b] upgrade — kill-triggered bonus damage increased from [b]1% → 3%[/b], but killer damage bonus raised to [b]20%[/b].[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Fix][/b] Resolved a problem where the [b]Freeze trait[/b]’s prerequisites would not function properly.[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Fix][/b] Corrected abnormal values after enhancing the [b]Freeze trait duration[/b].[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Optimization][/b] Ultimate Equipment: [b]“Jewel Recycling”[/b] upgrade — now the limit can be increased via Elemental Orbs.[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[Optimization][/b] Attempted fixes for various [b]multi-language issues[/b].[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Dodge, Gear Up, and Style Out – New Skins & Update Live!
notes.content:
[h1]Patch Notes – Update[/h1][p]Since launch, we’ve received tons of feedback and suggestions from players. We’ve been carefully recording everything and brainstorming improvements. Many of these will take time to fix, but here are the changes we were able to deliver in this update:[/p][hr][/hr][h2]🌀 About Perfect Dodge[/h2][p]In our game, if you dash into an enemy’s attack at the right moment, you can trigger a [b]Perfect Dodge[/b] with invincibility frames, giving you a chance to breathe.[/p][p]This mechanic is actually quite generous — especially against enemies with lingering hitboxes, you can almost trigger it 100% of the time.[/p][p]As a result, many boss attacks that look “over the top” are, in fact, free opportunities for players to trigger Perfect Dodges. The same goes for certain curses — when used correctly, what seemed like punishing attacks can actually become tools that help the player.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/026e64efbbae4eb06bbb182f1d444cd503c17e74.gif"][/img][/p][p]But here’s where we made a huge mistake: we never created a proper tutorial to teach players how to use Perfect Dodge.[/p][p]This caused many players in the early and mid-game to feel that bosses were overwhelmingly powerful, leaving them defenseless, frustrated, and locked into a “prison-like” experience. That’s on us, and we sincerely regret it.[/p][p]To address this, we’ve decided to [b]increase the Perfect Dodge window[/b] so it’s easier to trigger and avoid enemy moves.[/p][list][*][p]Perfect Dodge window increased from [b]10 frames → 15 frames[/b].
[i](Previously, Perfect Dodging melee attacks was a bit tough. It should now feel noticeably easier.)[/i][/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]🎮 Gameplay[/h2][list][*][p]Added a new [b]Dual-Element Synergy: Blood + Fire[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Added [b]4 new Ultimate Equipment[/b] and [b]1 new regular equipment[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]The Compendium now includes entries for [b]Elemental Synergies[/b] and [b]Ultimate Equipment[/b]. (Finally, you can check them all in one place!)[/p][/*][*][p]Adjusted an invisible-attacking enemy — its damage was too high and has been reduced.[/p][/*][*][p]Improved the [b]Reforge[/b] UX: after reforging, the cursor/focus will stay on the “Reforge” button, no need to move it back.[/p][/*][*][p]Reforge mechanic update: reforged Insectoid Cores will no longer generate duplicate elements.
[i](If you keep reforging without removing the core, you will eventually get the element you want.)[/i][/p][/*][*][p]Fusion mechanic update: the resulting core will always inherit one of the elements used as material. The more of one element you use, the higher the chance it becomes the final result.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a confirmation prompt when dismantling [b]red-quality Insectoid Cores[/b] that are already socketed, to prevent accidents.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]🎨 Skins[/h2][p]We’ve seen your enthusiasm for cosmetic skins. Even though sales are still far from 100k, we’ve decided to release [b]two new skins[/b] early as a thank-you gift for your support and patience. [i]Bows deeply![/i][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/a87313d00a4c1906d8dd9785649d553bee422f3b.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][h2]✨ Visual & FX[/h2][list][*][p]Added a new VFX to the [b]“Wind Dash” Insectoid Core trait[/b] (the one that enables infinite dashing). It now has clearer visuals when triggered.[/p][/*][*][p]Temporarily hidden certain “air distortion” effects (hit, level-up, portal FX) to avoid screen tearing and excessive visual noise.[/p][/*][*][p]Enemy ground poison pools now have more obvious visuals, making them easier to avoid.[/p][/*][*][p]Improved visuals for hit effects and level-up effects.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed portal FX causing screen tearing.[/p][/*][*][p]Heavy Attack now shows a “breathing light” effect when it’s ready (based on player feedback about unclear cooldown states).[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where ground items sometimes flickered on the Steam Deck.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]🐞 Bug Fixes[/h2][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where screen shake settings wouldn’t save properly.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed incorrect display in Insectoid Core description boxes.[/p][/*][*][p]Attempted a fix for lost save files.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed several equipment-related issues.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Major Update: Dual-Element Synergy & Ultimate Equipment Unleashed
notes.content: [p]Hello everyone![/p][p]We’ve received so much passionate feedback from our players. We’ve gone through each comment and suggestion, and while the game has already improved, we realized the overall experience still felt incomplete.[/p][p]So we pushed ourselves hard, worked overtime, and finally brought you [b]two brand-new core systems[/b] that were unfinished at launch. We believe the game now feels much more complete — and only then can we properly review and refine all your feedback.[/p][p]⚠️ This is not the end! Optimizing the game experience will be our long-term mission.[/p][hr][/hr][h2]🌌 New Major System #1: Dual-Element Synergy[/h2][p]Introducing the [b]Dual-Element Synergy system[/b]![/p][list][*][p]When you achieve a [b]4+4 combination of two elements[/b], a hidden synergy effect may be activated.[/p][/*][*][p]This allows two previously independent affinity systems to interact and create exciting new effects![/p][/*][*][p]All elements now have meaningful combinations.[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/2a229a1fb49d885a857b860aa20280ec970f740c.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/d7ae2afb6c90c75b6d1cf33a82d4de50fc116245.gif"][/img][/p][p][b]Current synergies include:[/b] Gold + Fire, Gold + Ice, Gold + Dark, Gold + Time, Wood + Fire, Wood + Ice, Wood + Gold, Wood + Earth, Wind + Thunder, Wind + Fire, Wind + Gold, Wind + Earth, Water + Ice, Water + Time, Water + Blood, Water + Earth, Thunder + Fire, Thunder + Dark, Thunder + Water, Thunder + Earth, Fire + Ice, Ice + Wind, Ice + Time, …and the [b]Ultimate Five-Element Synergy[/b] (2 Gold + 2 Wood + 2 Water + 2 Fire + 2 Earth).[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/d6d4ab05b5000071e458107d390b8ff1bb07e415.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/50307522504c166e7c70bb6c80a7e02234c07b7d.gif"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][h2]⚔️ New Major System #2: Ultimate Equipment[/h2][p]Defeat the Stage 4 boss to obtain a special device.[/p][list][*][p]Once picked up, you’ll unlock a new [b]Ultimate Equipment NPC[/b] in your [b]base[/b].[/p][/*][*][p](Note: You’ll need to defeat the Stage 4 boss again after updating.)[/p][/*][/list][p]⚠️ Warning! ⚠️ Ultimate Equipment is extremely powerful and game-changing.[/p][list][*][p]Currently, there are [b]26 Ultimate Equipment items[/b] (and more will be added in the future).[/p][/*][*][p]Each piece of Ultimate Equipment usually comes with [b]massive bonuses — but also massive drawbacks[/b]. Players will need to weigh their choices carefully.[/p][/*][*][p]Equipping one can completely transform your entire run.[/p][/*][*][p]They are [b]optional[/b] — you don’t have to use them if you prefer not to.[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/b81334d1406d1e62aad43ff3671a6b09b7164b57.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][h2]🔧 Other Improvements[/h2][h3]Equipment & Synergy Balance[/h3][list][*][p]No equipment or synergy was nerfed. Everything was either [b]buffed[/b] or [b]clarified[/b].[/p][/*][/list][h3]Gameplay Experience[/h3][list][*][p]Rage Attack animation no longer consumes time during Perfect Dodge slowdown.[/p][/*][*][p]All [b]Insectoid Core[/b] stat values have been unified. Even Common (white) cores now scale to the same strength as Legendary ones.[/p][/*][*][p]Dark Crystal Core drops slightly increased (30–90, up from 30–60).[/p][/*][*][p]Increased post-hit invincibility frames (from 60 → 70).[/p][/*][*][p]The game now auto-pauses when alt-tabbed.[/p][/*][*][p]Save screen now shows [b]clear count[/b] instead of death count.[/p][/*][*][p]Enemy hitbox adjustments: some monsters’ damage zones were mismatched with visuals, partial fixes applied. (Please keep sending feedback if you find more!)[/p][/*][/list][h3]Bug Fixes[/h3][list][*][p]Fixed occasional texture issues with [b]Shadow Clone[/b]; performance also optimized to reduce lag.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed Ice Insectoid Core 5th-tier synergy so it now correctly spawns under enemies.[/p][/*][/list][h3]Visual Effects[/h3][list][*][p]Water Element Tier 2 “Wave Rider” effect improved.[/p][/*][*][p]Super Armor effect made more visually obvious on enemies.[/p][/*][*][p]Some item icons updated.[/p][/*][*][p]Added many new VFX for elemental synergies.[/p][/*][*][p]Improved unlock screen effects for weapons and skins.[/p][/*][/list][h3]Audio & Music[/h3][list][*][p]Golden Axe SFX tuned down (less noisy).[/p][/*][*][p]Standard monster death SFX improved.[/p][/*][*][p]Added lots of new BGM: now most areas have [b]two or more tracks[/b] that play randomly.[/p][/*][*][p]Elite rooms now each have unique BGM.[/p][/*][*][p]Final Boss BGM replaced with a new track.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]💬 Final Words[/h2][p]This is our [b]first major content update since launch[/b] — with two new systems, tons of buffs, and many quality-of-life improvements.[/p][p]We know the road ahead is long, and this is just the beginning. But we’re committed to making the game fairer, smoother, and more fun with every update.[/p][p]Thank you for all your feedback and support — keep it coming, and we’ll keep improving![/p][p]Last but not least, if you’re enjoying the game, leaving a review on Steam really helps us a lot!![/p][p]– [b]Ethereal Fish Studio[/b][/p]

notes.title: Patch Notes – First-Day Hotfix
notes.content:
[p]Hello everyone! This is [b]Ethereal Fish Studio[/b]!
After launch, we received our very first wave of player feedback—thank you so much for all your suggestions! We pulled an all-nighter to fix as much as we could, aiming to bring you the best gameplay experience possible.[/p][p]Some bigger changes will take more time, but we prioritized solving the most painful issues first. Here’s a rundown of what’s new in this update:[/p][hr][/hr][h3]\[Stage 1 Boss Adjustments][/h3][list][*][p]Boss HP reduced by [b]20–30%[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]The tracking knife-throw skill will [b]no longer appear on lower difficulties[/b]—it now only shows up on higher ones.[/p][/*][/list][p][i](Now one burst of rage and this guy’s basically done for—time to vent your frustrations!)[/i][/p][hr][/hr][h3]\[Stage 3 Boss Adjustments][/h3][list][*][p]HP reduced by [b]20–30%[/b].[/p][/*][/list][p][i](We’ll keep monitoring to see if it still feels like a damage sponge!)[/i][/p][hr][/hr][h3]\[Meta Progression Order Adjustment][/h3][p]There’s an important talent that allows players to [b]refresh the 3-choice Insectoid Core selection[/b].
Previously, it was locked behind clearing later difficulties—terrible idea, our bad.[/p][p]Now, as long as you [b]reach Stage 2 on Difficulty 1[/b], this talent can be unlocked in the meta progression![/p][p][i](Honestly, what were we thinking putting this so late? Regret!)[/i][/p][hr][/hr][h3]\[Stage 4 Boss Adjustments][/h3][list][*][p]This boss also had a tracking knife-throw move.[/p][/*][*][p]Now, it [b]won’t appear before Difficulty 3[/b].[/p][/*][/list][p][i](Lowering the execution burden—giving everyone some breathing room.)[/i][/p][hr][/hr][h3]\[Shadow Blade Exclusive Trait Buffs][/h3][p]The following Shadow Blade traits have all been strengthened:[/p][list][*][p]Shadow Reap[/p][/*][*][p]Dark Surge[/p][/*][*][p]Godslayer[/p][/*][*][p]Shadow Assault[/p][/*][/list][p][i](We’ll keep monitoring and continue adjusting any weapons that feel off.)[/i][/p][hr][/hr][h3]\[In-Run Healing Improvements][/h3][list][*][p]Elite enemies now drop [b]healing potions that restore 30% HP[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Boss healing potions increased from [b]30% → 50% HP[/b].[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3]\[Probability Tweaks][/h3][list][*][p]The chance of starting with an [b]Epic-quality Insectoid Core[/b] has been increased from [b]2.9% → 3.5%[/b].[/p][/*][/list][p][i](Yes, it’s still random, and the weighted algorithm is complicated—so 3.5% doesn’t exactly mean 3.5%. But trust us, it’s definitely higher!)[/i][/p][hr][/hr][h3]\[Stage 2 Big-Eye Elite][/h3][p]This elite’s moveset was weird, its damage way too high, and many players suffered for it.
Turns out it was a [b]backend bug[/b] causing the damage spike. This has now been fixed.[/p][p][i](Let’s monitor it again and see how it feels?)[/i][/p][hr][/hr][h3]\[Other Fixes & Adjustments][/h3][list][*][p]Fixed another small crab-like enemy that had the same “overdamage” bug as above.[/p][/*][*][p]Removed the “Add to Wishlist” button from inside the game.[/p][/*][*][p]Changed the color of the “Reforge” button in the synthesis UI to make it stand out more. (Temporary fix—we’ll improve it further later.)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Optimized some sound effects[/b] for a smoother experience.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3]\[Final Words][/h3][p]We deeply regret the rough first-day experience, which went against our core vision of delivering a [b]爽游 (purely fun and satisfying game)[/b].[/p][p]But we will change it. We will fix it. We absolutely promise.[/p][p]Please give us a little more time—we’re a small team with limited manpower, but we will not let you down![/p]

(Odd numbers matter at last!)[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/6ea8baad044d10b41944191158302cf67ee15bf1.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]More Content & Improvements[/h2][list][*][p][b]New meta talents[/b]—grind them hard to grow stronger (though you can still win without them).[/p][/*][*][p][b]Equipment balance updates[/b] + [b]brand-new gear[/b] to discover.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Legendary Core at the start[/b]—no need to unlock it through talents anymore.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Improved scoring system[/b]—getting that triple-S now takes real skill.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Optimizations everywhere[/b]: text, UI, maps, sounds, and lots of bug fixes.[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/4bd6dc2cf4839a527a05da2ccb275d4b54a5bff0.gif"][/img][/p][h2]last but not least: Launch Discount!![/h2][p]We’re kicking things off with a [b]10% launch discount[/b], available for [b]14 days only[/b]. Don’t miss it—time to jump in![/p][p]Thank you all for your support throughout Early Access. This is just the beginning—we can’t wait to see your runs, builds, and feedback!!![/p][p][/p][p]Our discord: [url="https://discord.gg/KRmryFsTkJ"]https://discord.gg/KRmryFsTkJ[/url][/p][p]Our X: [url="https://x.com/StarFire_game"]https://x.com/StarFire_game[/url][/p][p]Our website: [url="https://indieherbgames.com/"]https://indieherbgames.com/[/url] [/p][p][/p]

notes.title: The major update for demo 2.0 is here!
notes.content: [p]Hello players, this is [b]ethereal fish studio[/b][/p][h2][b]After a few months of silence, we're here to share some major progress with you.[/b][/h2][p]To put it simply: we've completely reworked the game's core gameplay and overall structure. If you've played our previous demo, then congratulations, [b]you're about to experience a "brand new" game.[/b][/p][p]We'd like to start with a system you might be familiar with.[/p][p][b]【Combat Evolution: From "Rage Ultimate" to "Fury Attack"】[/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/ac21e131df7a4b9173f5485cad06f8c3de0b909c.gif"][/img][/p][p]Remember the old Rage system? You'd fill up a bar to unleash a single, powerful attack.[/p][p][b]Now, it has evolved.[/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/a04efcca92372ec386ec36a72ff915bccc4acad0.gif"][/img][/p][p]We've upgraded it to a three-segment energy bar. Each use consumes only one segment and has its own dedicated button, so you'll no longer trigger it by accident when using a heavy attack.[/p][p]But that's just the basics. The real highlight is that once you've stored all three segments, you can unleash the true ultimate skill with a specific command: the "Fury Attack."[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/4bd6dc2cf4839a527a05da2ccb275d4b54a5bff0.gif"][/img][/p][p]This new mechanic is just the tip of the iceberg of our massive updates. Next, we want to talk about some deeper changes.[/p][p][b]【On the UI: A Much-Needed Overhaul】[/b][/p][p]To be honest, we don't have anyone on our team who specializes in UI design. The UI in the previous version was... rather hastily put together, and we received a lot of complaints about it.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/c9e52ebd9ce7f99b287c76ab1e31444314a099c5.png"][/img][/p][p]At first, we thought that as a "poor" indie dev team, players might be more forgiving. But it turns out that a clean UI is crucial for the overall game experience.[/p][p]So this time, we were determined to make a change. We hired a professional UI designer to completely remake the game's entire user interface.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/09379bf25c54b735c11fc3b0b43cbefe92395ed0.png"][/img][/p][p]The new UI finally makes the game look like a "proper game." We hope you'll be happy with the new design.[/p][p][b]【Core Gameplay: A Complete Restructure】[/b][/p][h2][b]Now for the main event of this update: the complete overhaul of the core gameplay.[/b][/h2][p]The old progression system revolved around "level up, pick a weapon, pick an upgrade." The advantage was its simplicity, but the disadvantage was also clear: the experience was relatively monotonous, with limited room for players to create their own builds.[/p][p]We want every run of the game to offer more strategic depth and randomness.[/p][p]So, we reworked the "Insectoid Core" system.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/3e0fb3de6f553a51f9e0ba6a78a4b186506cbdff.png"][/img][/p][p]Previously, Insectoid Cores mostly provided simple stat bonuses. Now, we've given them various elemental properties like Cryo, Pyro, and Dendro. When you collect a certain number of cores of the same element, you'll activate powerful "Affinity" effects.[/p][p]For example:[/p][p][b]Equip two "Cryo Cores"[/b]: An ice ring appears at your character's feet, with a chance to freeze enemies on hit.[/p][p]·[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/ccf298a6d7409c2d77583aa525d513bd0e7612a8.gif"][/img][/p][p][b]Equip two "Dendro Cores"[/b]: Vines will automatically seek out and attack enemies.[/p][p]·[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/3114c699fe51bbc72ccaa7fb29036466c3412f2f.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]The highest-tier Red Insectoid Cores come with powerful unique effects that can fundamentally change the strength of your build. This way, figuring out the optimal combination based on the cores you get in each run becomes a new source of fun and challenge.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/8335ee1edb688504d230ff0ad0bbbabffe8a85ff.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]To allow for free experimentation, we've also redesigned the inventory system. Insectoid Cores must be socketed to take effect, and they can be freely removed and swapped at any time.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/4157b156c1febda9d4a9e64472688575d2b599cd.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]If you get a core you don't want, you can combine it into a higher-tier one at the shop, or dismantle it for materials to reforge and reroll for the affixes you need. We want to give players enough agency to build their ideal character step by step.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/07e3caf28a79a906f18df520b90a4a815e75f7f1.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]By the way, the old weapon upgrade system has also been reworked. It's no longer tied to your level but now appears as a "unique affix" on high-tier Red Insectoid Cores, which can also be socketed or removed at will. No more being locked into a choice for the rest of the run.[/p][p][b]【And There's More...】[/b][/p][p]In addition to these core changes, we've made many other optimizations and additions:[/p][p][b]Equipment System[/b]: We've removed some stat-stick items and added more new equipment with unique mechanics.[/p][p]·[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/bdddb5f7e8c7558a63d29f6e5a4c73c8fcefef17.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]Meta-progression[/b]: We've added an out-of-run progression system. But don't worry, its purpose is to make the game more enjoyable, not to gate your progress.[/p][p]·[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45145657/0901ac61ca4210617c22f550881565157ec6e596.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]Other[/b]: We've also added a base, streamlined damage types, optimized the room reward mechanics, and more...[/p][p]Our goal with all these changes is simple: [b]to raise the gameplay ceiling and enrich the game's content.[/b][/p][p][/p][p][b]The brand new Demo 2.0 is now available for download[/b], where you can experience most of these changes firsthand. (Of course, we've still saved some surprises for the full release.) Stay tuned for major news about the official launch next month~[/p][p][/p][p]We eagerly await your discussions and suggestions in the comments. Every piece of feedback you provide is [b]invaluable motivation that helps us make the game better.[/b][/p][p]Thank you for your patience and for reading.[/p][h1]— ethereal fish studio[/h1][p] [/p]

notes.title: Dev Interview: The Story Behind Star Fire: Eternal Cycle
notes.content:
[p][i]Note: This interview was originally published on December 24, 2024, by Grape Games — one of China’s leading video game media outlets. We’ve translated it into English and are sharing it here with the Steam Community ahead of the upcoming Star Fire: Eternal Cycle demo.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Faced with the shutdown of projects or even entire departments, what would you choose — transfer to another team and stay in the company, or take the severance package and pursue something new? Jensen, the producer of [i]Star Fire: Eternal Cycle[/i], clearly chose the latter.[/p][p]At this year’s WePlay Expo, I visited the [i]Star Fire[/i] booth and had a hands-on experience with their demo.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXekz-UUjtctxm2VNs3VVmB27BKugaruPCl6XDmdwqHTLUAP1srfZZE3bAZ-AwtidCCy-fE58AvLDaUa9FdU1gjs5EAVNklKKmHl1ngxI0ZOFt54KHsCnEo8JxEKUoC2X2zyKxfOBbxfQ_jwF8zZFA?key=uLDH3pLtt-ayqiO6CqHK4Q"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]This side-scrolling roguelike action game lets players attack, dodge, and move freely while combining primary and secondary weapons to create unique builds. As players progress through monster rooms, challenge rooms, and reward chambers, they accumulate power to survive increasingly intense boss battles.[/p][p]If we were to compare it to existing roguelikes, [i]Star Fire: Eternal Cycle[/i] shares a similar feel to [i]Hades[/i], especially in its focus on fluid combat and precise dodging.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXf_b-I02ewXRPaJiZP_sct9ZDesYW3BRupOeUJtC-TpZ_13JYu172F0Oyww-kgynapiDf58DNs1xBju0CE1poizdkoRgmw4VKS5-d335OdAqEro8iR4bacY1fXmF-HF7pki1yKPAwdURTVCba5_yQ?key=uLDH3pLtt-ayqiO6CqHK4Q"][/img][/p][p]At the same time, [i]Star Fire[/i] incorporates deep build mechanics—stats, attack types, skill effects—adding layers of strategy to the action core.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXd1bPVVB02QTi852llJ55POtw58D_1ZfB074r0poxXcUji2BYCEbH8caBnsMgCDwTBMiJKfPhaREm7rRrq3TIThq9ftkQ_kmGRmHdkYLdvA6Ug1seF9Vk5vWkisfv5hQ_FcA70yds7fSJ-MBWsLtHg?key=uLDH3pLtt-ayqiO6CqHK4Q"][/img][/p][p]Between play sessions, I had a brief chat with Jensen. Unlike many indie devs who are fresh graduates or junior designers, Jensen is a veteran with over a decade of experience at top-tier studios. He once led development on [i]Metal Revolution[/i] at NExT Studios, which secured a $3 million publishing deal from Yoozoo Interactive.[/p][p]Since leaving Tencent last year, Jensen formed a six-person team and has fully devoted himself to developing [i]Star Fire[/i]. Over the past two years, not only has the team taken no salary—they’ve poured nearly RMB 1 million into the project. [/p][p]The game is still in development and expected to release in 2025. [/p][p]But why leave a major studio to go indie? Why choose the ultra-competitive roguelike genre for their debut title? And how has Jensen’s mindset changed over time?[/p][p]To answer these questions, I visited the Star Fire team at their studio, Free & Salty Fish (a direct translation from Chinese), and had an in-depth conversation with Jensen.[/p][p] [/p][h2][b]01[/b][/h2][h2][b]Unorthodox Beginnings[/b][/h2][p]I was curious — why name the studio “Ethereal Fish”?[/p][p]Jensen explained that he wanted the team to work in a relaxed and unburdened state, just like the studio’s name implies. Their goal isn’t to chase success at all costs, but to enjoy doing what they love — and if they make some money along the way, great. As long as the work is fulfilling, everything else will follow naturally.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcw1q9rmFzw3co-rK2s0vBrQcFnOeUYJM96E7iS-yuWgZkdCaD6TBBBp5ODRB8tumTXpl_K9lEpD4ZtSrtKDhn-Mp0dVlc5-aX_bqcSRgJBZx6uBkV3ULgizkfKfRgxrfmdVprLLFH-fVidNbyE3g?key=uLDH3pLtt-ayqiO6CqHK4Q"][/img][/p][p]Ironically, this laid-back philosophy is in stark contrast to what originally drew Jensen into the industry more than a decade ago: the belief that making games was an easy way to make money.[/p][p]At the time, China’s single-player PC games were in decline, the mobile game boom hadn’t yet taken off, and online MMORPGs like [i]World of Warcraft[/i] and [i]ZT Online[/i] dominated the market.[/p][p]According to Jensen, he got into the industry through a rather unorthodox path.[/p][p]The story begins when he dropped out of high school. One day, he spotted a newspaper ad recruiting “game developers.” Intrigued, he followed up, only to learn that the ad was actually for a paid game development training course, not a job.[/p][p]Though disappointed, Jensen still enrolled — desperate to break into the gaming industry and earn a living. He trained for less than half a year, learning the basics of game animation.[/p][p]To help students get hands-on experience (and perhaps to make use of free labor), the school set up its own outsourcing company, offering a pipeline from training to employment. The pay was low, but Jensen said he gained valuable experience during that time.[/p][p]After training, he joined a small studio doing animation outsourcing. Then came a job at Giant Network, followed by five years at Kingsoft, where he worked on titles like [i]JX3 Online[/i] and [i]Swordsman World[/i] (mobile). Around 2017, he landed at Tencent.[/p][p]One of the projects he contributed to at Tencent was the mobile version of [i]Fantasy Westward Journey[/i].[/p][p]Over the years, Jensen had worked on both mobile and MMO projects, but eventually he realized that animation alone no longer satisfied his creative ambitions.[/p][p]On the one hand, animation has limitations in game development — it always serves the game’s larger systems. On the other, the industry culture frustrated him. Despite nearly a decade of experience, he often found himself taking orders from freshly graduated junior designers.[/p][p]It was during his time at Kingsoft that Jensen began studying game engines in his spare time. Unity was just gaining traction, and he dove into online tutorials to self-learn.[/p][p]He taught himself how to make a character move, attack, and interact with enemies. To test his progress, he built several small demos.[/p][p]One of them — a side-scrolling mobile fighting game — stood out. Having previously worked on [i]League of Stickman[/i], a small but successful action title, Jensen initially wanted to build something similar.[/p][p]But he quickly realized that the mobile action platformer space was crowded and ultra-competitive. Instead, he pivoted toward making a pure fighting game.[/p][p]As an animator, he’d long dreamed of creating a fighting title. At the time, only a few fighting games like [i]Shadow Fight[/i] existed on mobile. He played them and thought, “The controls feel terrible. I can definitely do better than this.”[/p][p]That demo eventually evolved into [i]Metal Revolution[/i], which would become the sixth officially greenlit project at NExT Studios.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdu1o-PbNjE5kLHsD8afCSpjok-kAQGdljQYb3f4Jia-ja1upKpNkMpL_WvXS8m7hc5dFm38SQeDQWTVW2nWRj39FE5ibRXZpcbGH_Nrt5rot63I6zXd0eECp9K4prRRjrrJh5NwAxX6ExFi5-e-Zs?key=uLDH3pLtt-ayqiO6CqHK4Q"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]02[/b][/h2][h2][b]Metal Revolution[/b][/h2][p]After joining Tencent, Jensen continued developing his fighting game demo in his spare time while also attending internal knowledge-sharing sessions.[/p][p]It was during one of these sessions — a lecture on overseas publishing strategies — that he met Moliba, the presenter. She was surprised to see someone from the art department attending, since such events were usually filled with designers and programmers, not artists.[/p][p]Later, Moliba transferred from Tencent’s global publishing division to NExT Studios. One day, Jensen saw a recruitment post from her on WeChat and reached out. She introduced him to Steven Wu (Wu Yujun), the head of NExT’s Shenzhen branch at the time.[/p][p]Jensen presented his fighting game demo to Steven, who was impressed by how polished and visually striking it was. Steven believed it had real potential and wanted to develop it into a full project.[/p][p]So around 2018, Jensen officially joined NExT Studios.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdMuYUAcZtaOPSxqQbsRsXSr1EniD9IohdWqB6Xu4lL-WxHgm3VPbYvcXwNpLqEFgBykmHSfML_JKM_GUoyEuvMOMZfIZRMlz5sqnoVoARlGwfvbjWHTy9qFXENkF26LXnEhRrWP6JS5ojhRlaOsMk?key=uLDH3pLtt-ayqiO6CqHK4Q"][/img][/p][p]Early on, [i]Metal Revolution[/i] was developed as a mobile game. For ease of testing and showcasing, the team also packaged a PC version. To their surprise, the PC version received strong feedback at events and from players.[/p][p]After further internal validation, they decided to launch on PC first, with mobile and possibly console versions to follow, depending on the market response.[/p][p]According to Jensen, [i]Metal Revolution[/i] — a hardcore, niche 1v1 mech fighting game — faced internal skepticism from the beginning. During the first internal review, he and the evaluators couldn’t reach a consensus. Ultimately, the game’s strong visuals and satisfying combat effects helped it secure official greenlight status. But that was just the first of many challenges.[/p][p]As the studio matured, NExT realized that letting every team pursue purely creative projects wasn’t sustainable. They reorganized: a select group of employees with strong creative drive formed a special incubator team, while others shifted to more commercially driven, top-down projects focused on retention, monetization, and GaaS (Games as a Service) models.[/p][p]Under this new structure, [i]Metal Revolution[/i] had to adjust its roadmap — setting KPIs, calculating ROI, and adding character progression systems. It also transitioned back from PC to mobile.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfA5SM6psWa1gVzUpuBgm5dUtOWT7-jpMSnhEgQc5CW_GJNBIAr8jHzgAK3IUQq13EaNP4GsHDfdGAr8v33zrBrjN4Wan87f1-7mKDISt5OutPTYUForOqRokwe9RTgvNZ6tIA4wkxbJx36d1ziYas?key=uLDH3pLtt-ayqiO6CqHK4Q"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Jensen felt this pivot was fundamentally misaligned with the game’s DNA. From the outset, [i]Metal Revolution[/i] was never designed to chase commercial trends. Now, it was being pressured to meet KPIs. Its monetization relied on selling characters, but the fighting game audience was too niche to support aggressive revenue goals.[/p][p]Still, despite the challenges, [i]Metal Revolution[/i] managed to land a significant milestone: it secured a $3 million publishing advance from Yoozoo Interactive.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcC0N_zVR_R5q59XDLKr4XUFAjIgco4JKtM5OITYCg-3IU-O1XHZYr_fPSYaKX0ZXaJcodOZ19ReT7leWJsUCmm6X29kRJurFHgcY1qgwPXsZR1GFEN4SI23jWABf646RPTZ6LMBXiBXEEN3YJMpA?key=uLDH3pLtt-ayqiO6CqHK4Q"][/img][/p][p]In August 2021, the game launched in open beta across 12 South American countries, topping the free game charts on Google Play in Brazil and beyond. It had also received a publishing license in China and secured a domestic publisher.[/p][p]Unfortunately, [i]Metal Revolution[/i] may never officially launch in China.[/p][p]At the end of 2022, NExT’s general manager Shen Li suddenly left the company. Starting in 2023, NExT began a wave of restructuring: the creative incubator was disbanded, its head Zhang Zhechuan resigned, the producer of [i]SYNCED[/i] moved to another team, and vice president Gu Yu also departed. Jensen’s [i]Metal Revolution[/i] team was among those affected.[/p][p]During our conversation, I noticed that Jensen struggled to recall specific dates — when he entered the industry, how long he’d worked, when he joined NExT, and how long the project took.[/p][p]“I’m not very sensitive to time,” he admitted.[/p][p]Except for one date: April 17, 2023 — his last day at NExT.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcKAdjQIzdsfmsGem5JnaQk8YxfCTefJB7b-vefp9x7CXnZGL9r19a0K_XMV7y743w0hjmOIuS_udhW_iyexm0DccBxBwh4jOuW29fyG_lWVYKKz-ayotKwfiP2-0Cr1Xf2-J_nlwifJmyi-hkFPyg?key=uLDH3pLtt-ayqiO6CqHK4Q"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]03[/b]
[b]Star Fire: Eternal Cycle[/b][/h2][p]Looking back, Jensen believes there were two main reasons [i]Metal Revolution[/i] was ultimately canceled: first, organizational restructuring at the studio; second, the game’s revenue didn’t meet expectations.[/p][p]He broke it down for me: based on Tencent’s internal cost structure, a 10-person team at RMB 1 million per person annually meant the game cost at least RMB 10 million per year. With nearly five years of development, the total cost was likely over RMB 50 million. YooZoo’s $3 million advance? It only covered about two years.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXebinbvf2LzTIRZPhOKmhQaDxb1XqSRLqCBu08FckDgoxvaYwjJyGKtTdsEZKKW9MYHO2UVINKT5YRoKCgWiR1_nNtdKSHeSR3qFOr_RfpEV-7XZo7Frw5d9YjStk-Fk394m1JXznPKfK-ZKEsXpH0?key=uLDH3pLtt-ayqiO6CqHK4Q"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]So why did he choose to walk away rather than transfer to another team? Jensen explained:[/p][p]On one hand, even if he joined another team, he would likely remain “just a cog in the machine.” One person’s impact is limited. But if a group of like-minded people came together and started something of their own, the value they could create might be entirely different.[/p][p]On the other hand, intellectual properties (IP) can grow with time. Take [i]Street Fighter[/i], for example. It started decades ago and gradually gained a devoted fanbase through sequels. Jensen wanted to build something like that too.[/p][p]So, with his severance package in hand, Jensen left the high-paced tech hub of Tencent’s Science Park and rented a 100-square-meter office in the outskirts of Shenzhen’s Guangming District for RMB 10,000 per month. There, he began his new life — as a "free and salty fish."[/p][p]Each morning, after dropping his kid off at school, Jensen arrives at the office around 7 or 8 a.m., working until 5 or 6 in the evening. “If I feel inspired, I’ll stay longer. If not, I’ll go home and take care of my kid.”[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdUqeocIpx9MmSEsgUT8LmSyNdnGddGb40tixnTkjY7yf5eGEpEwfimmFgE7BWiwcXKz-VZESjqvPJ40ycOrrzBA2q2tX1r5wSuArACiqzvLc-C4AVnEiHsgyqY4sPx7elRjcF0ouNdVZFl3812a7Q?key=uLDH3pLtt-ayqiO6CqHK4Q"][/img][/p][p]For his team, the daily routine isn’t that different from working at a company. Back at Tencent, Jensen led a team with a hands-off style: as long as people delivered, he gave them freedom. Now, with his own studio, it’s much the same — no fixed hours, just get the work done.[/p][p]He even set up a play area in the office for his kid to hang out.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfij4S82sB-Bmg70HDUHh1GZ5HVwiQw4oRMh31RM85Ssvmu0vSrgf12UbINiDiafQ10WAicR5bOtiTQyN6NuigLE7ZxP9Jlqh5a-AiRgao7nAucOpsEw_CKuVCPWhsPT1SVS5Zgz6NYeZSGdS-S7A?key=uLDH3pLtt-ayqiO6CqHK4Q"][/img][/p][p]As for the new project, the team chose to make a roguelike action game. They felt that traditional genres like fighting games or MMORPGs were already saturated and hard to break into. Roguelikes, being newer and more immersive, offered a better chance to hook players.[/p][p]Plus, their background in fighting game development gave them confidence in the action gameplay. Ironically, this experience also tripped them up at the beginning.[/p][p]Take basic attacks, for example. Initially, they added hit-stop effects to give each strike a satisfying impact — a common technique in fighting games. But players complained that the animations felt stiff and the controls unresponsive.[/p][p]That’s when the team realized something important: the design priorities for fighting games and roguelike action games are fundamentally different. The former requires strict frame data, animation timing, and combo limitations. The latter emphasizes speed, fluidity, and freedom of movement — in short, the difference between 1v1 combat and 1vMany.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdz2z1arP-DrE7qyLs58SDcvQnvLhG3INIuFdRlRtfDPMggBQDmRlVykxYjqZhn6MllJca9VKJ_OWfJgA0iFWFtbakyyLqjTDb0Y9GMs9CKShCXwedlCiNtEMHY5VzVnon2jCYtgN1u2eFHIqEKav4?key=uLDH3pLtt-ayqiO6CqHK4Q"][/img][/p][p][i]Translation (left to right): Early Build · Mid Build · Current Build[/i][/p][p][/p][p]One of the hardest challenges over the past two years has been balancing action and build mechanics.[/p][p]Jensen cited two contrasting examples: [i]Hades[/i], which leans more toward action — players can clear the game with just solid gameplay and minor build decisions; and [i]Warm Snow[/i], which is more about constructing an overpowered build, where the right card combo can trivialize combat.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdaXIuWzw-X9m5lkBn8nPi50_DljCgIAyCU6dCLSjw549t_E2QvtLiPQn920M5xa7HlgGwrcGGazyVyDVNaoCCNITagzfc-b-42BByd9sIQeJ0DDRSafAjmLjuqFksMg3Id73kBKjav2tm9USDcnTM?key=uLDH3pLtt-ayqiO6CqHK4Q"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]These games offer very different experiences. By tweaking the ratio of action to build depth, developers can craft roguelikes that cater to different player preferences.[/p][p]Jensen’s team is now focused on playtesting and gathering feedback to strike the right balance in their own game.[/p][p]Of course, even without KPIs or PowerPoints, the team isn’t free of pressure.[/p][p]About three or four months ago, they reached out to publishers, but the feedback was underwhelming. After reflecting on it, Jensen concluded that the product simply wasn’t good enough.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfPuaW6QddUWosDT2E25tw19AL1gOq0sVML-0wudg7u7EVuAPfdy2PzHBqQe_39-joNsR6QjTIMPunuhiBd8duZM8_R4xFvj-dcYImsouBhSWW9LdjbmSw5V-JR2OsnSGMiJAv5Jw0MumbkfbbANh4?key=uLDH3pLtt-ayqiO6CqHK4Q"][/img][/p][p]They redirected their anxiety into improving the game, iterating non-stop for nearly two months. Eventually, just by releasing a new gameplay video, they drew the attention of multiple publishers — who now came to them, not the other way around.[/p][p]“Our takeaway was: if your game is awesome enough, you don’t need to chase people down — they’ll come to you. So our job is to make the game awesome, period.”[/p][p]To date, Ethereal Fish Studio has not accepted any investment or publishing deals. Over the last two years, the team hasn’t earned a cent — in fact, they’ve invested nearly RMB 1 million of their own money into the project.[/p][p]Naturally, some might wonder: is this lifestyle really sustainable? What if their savings run out? What if the game fails — will they all go back to corporate jobs?[/p][p]Jensen acknowledged those concerns. But he believes their timeline is still within reason. Most indie games take between 1.5 to 3 years to develop. They’re approaching the 2-year mark, which feels like a healthy median. But if it drags on to five years? “That would be a problem,” he said.[/p][p]From day one, Jensen made sure every team member understood the risks. “Risk and reward go hand in hand. If we succeed, we split the profits. If we fail, we share the losses. If someone isn’t ready for that, then the best choice is to stay at a company.”[/p][p][/p][h2][b]04[/b][/h2][h2][b]Final Thoughts[/b][/h2][p]Jensen told me that, compared to when he first left Tencent, his mindset hasn’t changed much. If anything, he’s just enjoying the process more now — because he feels like he’s growing stronger every day.[/p][p]In contrast to the corporate environment — where KPIs, managers, and publishers constantly impose constraints — he now receives player feedback and can immediately make adjustments. If something doesn’t feel right, he can fix it overnight.[/p][p]After attending WePlay, he found himself losing sleep — not from stress, but from the flurry of player feedback that sparked countless ideas. He couldn’t stop thinking about how to improve the game.[/p][p]In the comments section of their Bilibili page, many players have offered suggestions and ideas for improvement.[/p][p]At the end of our conversation, I asked Jensen, “What’s your expectation for this game?”[/p][p]“To be honest,” he said, “we just want to stay afloat. As long as we can survive, we’re good. We’re not expecting to launch a mega hit right out of the gate. First we live — then we build. And hopefully, we can keep doing what we find meaningful.”[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p]The journey’s just beginning. Look forward to the Star Fire: Eternal Cycle demo this August — and see what Jensen and the team have been building from the ground up.[/p][p][/p][p]Link to the original article in Chinese: [url="https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/eaZSLuVcRjTFhV6w7Kac6g"]https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/eaZSLuVcRjTFhV6w7Kac6g[/url][/p][p]Follow Jensen on X: [url="https://x.com/jensenhu3"]https://x.com/jensenhu3[/url][/p][p]Follow Star Fire: Eternal Cycle on X: [url="https://x.com/StarFire_game"]https://x.com/StarFire_game[/url][/p]

notes.title: Demo Version – Major Update Aug 2025
notes.content: [p]Star Fire is a love letter to classic arcade side-scrollers, reimagined with roguelite progression, modern action polish, and that “just one more run” itch. It’s fast, punchy, and all about no-pressure fun with tight combat, slick movement, and endless ways to cause chaos.[/p]
